title: Galois descent and scalar-extension detection for affine closed subgroups
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All groups below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$; subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $L/k$ be a Galois field extension, possibly infinite, meaning an algebraic normal separable extension. Let $J$ be an affine group scheme over $k$ and let $V\subseteq J_L=J\times_kL$ be a closed subgroup. The canonical semilinear action of $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)$ on $J_L$ acts on its coordinate algebra by $\sigma(a\otimes\lambda)=a\otimes\sigma(\lambda)$. If the defining ideal of $V$ in $\mathcal O(J)\otimes_kL$ is stable under this action, there is a unique closed subgroup $N\subseteq J$ with $N_L=V$ as subgroup schemes. For any field extension $K/k$, equality and inclusion of closed subgroup schemes of $J$ can be tested after extension to $K$. Normality can also be tested after field extension: $N$ is normal in $J$ if and only if $N_K$ is normal in $J_K$. Field extension uses [def-pc-field-extension]; normality means normality on $A$-points for every commutative base algebra $A$.

source.place: Section 1.54(a)–(b), printed pp.21–22 (descent of subgroups, including infinite Galois extensions); Appendix A.65–A.66. Inclusion and normality detection are faithfully flat detection of defining-ideal inclusions and of the conjugation factorization, the same affine descent criterion.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O(J)$ and let $I\subseteq A_L=A\otimes_kL$ be the defining ideal of $V$. Apply [lem-sfb-galois-stable-subspace-descent] to $M=A$ and $W=I$: its stability is precisely the hypothesis, and its $L$-linearity follows because it is an ideal. Thus $I$ is the $L$-span of $I_0\otimes1$, where $I_0=\{a\in A:a\otimes1\in I\}$. This $I_0$ is an ideal: it is closed under addition and, for $a\in I_0$, $b\in A$, $(ba)\otimes1=(b\otimes1)(a\otimes1)\in I$. The ideal generated by $I_0\otimes1$ equals this $L$-span: multiplication by $b\otimes\lambda$ takes $a\otimes1$ to $(ba)\otimes\lambda$, and pure tensors span $A_L$. Therefore $I=I_0A_L$.

source.place: A.64–A.65, printed pp.580–581, affine ideal descent underlying 1.54(b).

proof.text: Set $N=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I_0)\subseteq J$ using [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Its coordinate algebra is generated by the images of any finite algebra generating set for $A$, so $N$ is of finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], $(A/I_0)\otimes_k L\cong A_L/(I_0A_L)$: on pure tensors the map sends $\bar a\otimes\lambda$ to the class of $a\otimes\lambda$, while the reverse map is induced by $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar a\otimes\lambda$; both composites fix the algebra generators. The same tensor universal property identifies affine fibre products with spectra of tensor products (maps into them are pairs of compatible algebra maps). Consequently $N_L=V$ as closed subschemes, with their given embeddings in $J_L$.

For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] give an injection $R\hookrightarrow R_L=R\otimes_kL$. Under [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a point $x\in J(R)$ lies in $N(R)$ exactly when the map $x^\sharp:A\to R$ kills $I_0$. If its extension lies in $V(R_L)=N_L(R_L)$, each $x^\sharp(a)$ for $a\in I_0$ maps to zero in $R_L$ and is therefore zero in $R$. Thus membership is reflected. The identity of $J(R)$, the product of two points of $N(R)$, and the inverse of such a point extend to the corresponding identity, product and inverse in the subgroup $V(R_L)$; reflected membership puts all three in $N(R)$. By [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] this proves $N$ is a closed subgroup. This uses all base algebras $R$, including nonreduced ones, rather than just field-valued points.

source.place: 1.54(b), deduction from A.65–A.66, printed pp.21–22,581; affine pointwise verification of the subgroup assertion.

proof.text: For any field extension $K/k$ and ideals $P,Q\subseteq A$ of two closed subgroup schemes, write $P_K=PA_K$ and $Q_K=QA_K$. Their coordinate descriptions are given by [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the quotient tensor calculation of step 2, using [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat, lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], $P_K\cap A=P$ and $Q_K\cap A=Q$. Hence $P_K\subseteq Q_K$ implies $P\subseteq Q$; the converse follows directly by extending generators. Equality follows by applying both inclusions. Inclusion of closed subschemes reverses ideal inclusion: a map $A/Q\to A/P$ over $A$ exists exactly when $Q\subseteq P$, by the quotient universal property. This proves the inclusion and equality assertions. Taking $K=L$ proves uniqueness of the descended subgroup.

source.place: 1.54(a) and A.65 uniqueness, printed pp.21,581; inclusion is the same contraction argument (Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05CK, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective).

proof.text: Let $N$ now be any closed subgroup of $J$. If $N$ is normal, every commutative $K$-algebra $B$ is a $k$-algebra and $N_K(B)=N(B)$, $J_K(B)=J(B)$ by the base-change universal property [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] (a $K$-algebra map $A_K\to B$ is the same as a $k$-algebra map $A\to B$, and, for the defining ideal $P\subseteq A$ of $N$, it kills $PA_K$ exactly when the restriction kills $P$), so $N_K$ is normal. Conversely suppose $N_K$ is normal. For a $k$-algebra $R$, $g\in J(R)$ and $n\in N(R)$, extend them to $R_K=R\otimes_kK$. Normality there implies that the image of $gng^{-1}$ belongs to $N_K(R_K)$. A defining equation $a$ of $N$ therefore has value zero in $R_K$ on $gng^{-1}$. The injection $R\to R_K$, from [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat, lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], makes this value zero in $R$. Thus $gng^{-1}\in N(R)$ for all $R,g,n$, which is normality as defined in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Replacing $g$ by $g^{-1}$ gives equality of conjugate subgroups if desired. The ring-map description of points uses [def-weil-affine-spectrum], including its functoriality.

source.place: Affine equation-detection argument extending 1.54(a), A.65; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 05CK, lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective.
